Provider take-over — the screens

These are the screens a provider and an admin will see; it is not a single page.

Example used everywhere: the Clinket team built Joe's Plumbing (info@joesplumbing.com, 905-555-1234, no password); Asha's Bright Salon was built the same way and Asha has already taken it over. Each frame is drawn from the real screen in that app — its own layout, colours, sizes and icons — and the line under it names the file it copies. Web screens are shown at phone (375), iPad (820) and laptop (1280) width; scroll a row sideways to see every frame. Plan: Data/admin-provider-setup/PLAN.md §3, §4, §5 (S6), §8.

Main screenWaiting / in progressProblemOffline

1Register with the team's phone

Joe opens Register and types the phone number our team used (905-555-1234) with any email. Instead of an error, the form is replaced by this screen. One tap sends a code to that phone and opens the normal code screen with the number already filled in. Nothing on it shows the account's email or any other detail.

Provider web business.clinket.com/auth/register

Provider phone app clinqetmobilepartnerapp

Customer web clinket.com/auth/register — customer wording

Customer phone app clinqetmobileuserapp

2Code sign-in — "Resend Code" now works

The code screen stays exactly as it is. Today "Resend Code" fails for everyone who has not turned on two-step sign-in. After the fix it sends a fresh sign-in code, clears the boxes, starts the next wait (30 s, then 40 s, then 60 s) and says so.

Provider web /auth/login-verify-phone

Provider phone app · Customer web · Customer phone app

3Password sign-in failed — "No password yet? Sign in with a code"

The server answer does not change ("Invalid email or password", the same for every account, so nothing is given away). After any failed password the screen adds one line under it that opens code sign-in. Accounts our team made have no password, so this is how Joe finds his way in.

Provider web /auth/login-with-email

Provider phone app · Customer web · Customer phone app

4"Forgot password" on an account with only a phone

Today the app says a code was sent and nothing arrives. Now a text code arrives; once Joe types it he is signed straight in (a password needs an email to sign in with), and he sees this screen.

Provider web /auth/forgot-verify-phone → signed in

Provider phone app · Customer web · Customer phone app

5Settings — the menu says "Set Password" when there is none

The Set Password page already exists in all four apps and already switches itself when an account has no password. The only change: the menu entry that opens it now reads Set Password instead of "Change Password". If Joe signed in more than 10 minutes ago, the existing "sign in again" step runs first.

Provider web /dashboard/profile/change-password

Provider phone app · Customer web · Customer phone app

6Admin — "Providers you have added"

Each provider the team built now shows whether the owner has taken it over. Before take-over: Continue setup and Correct email / phone. After: Help with setup only (sign-in details are the owner's from then on).

Admin web /provider-accounts

Admin phone app clinqetmobileadminapp

7Admin — "Correct email / phone"

Only for an account the owner has not taken over yet. The new email or phone must not belong to any other Clinket account. No code is sent and nothing is sent to Joe; an audit line is written.

Admin web

Admin phone app — native bottom sheet

8Admin — inside a business: setup banner and the locked online-booking switch

The banner says plainly what the session allows and how long is left. While Joe has not taken over, online booking is forced off and the switch is locked with the reason. It turns on by itself the moment Joe signs in.

Admin web /provider-accounts/:userId/onboarding

Admin phone app

9Admin — the Exit box (only on an account the provider manages)

When the team helped Asha after she took over, pressing Exit asks once. The tick is on by default. Ticking the areas is optional and makes the notice specific; the line at the bottom shows exactly what Asha will see. Try it: tap the tick and the area chips in the first frame. On a business nobody has taken over yet, Exit leaves straight away as today.

Admin web

Admin phone app — native bottom sheet

10What Asha receives — one notice, "Your profile was updated"

One notice, in the app (live) and as a phone push. With one area ticked, tapping it opens that page; otherwise the dashboard. Nothing is sent if the box was unticked or the session ran out.

Provider web /dashboard/notifications

Provider phone app

WEvery new string, and where its words live

Provider and customer apps: one key per string in all five language files (en, es, fr, gu, hi). Admin web and admin phone are English-only by rule (CLAUDE.md §0.10). Lines marked server are already-translated sentences the server sends; the screens never write their own copy of them. Keys marked new are proposals — final names are chosen when the code is written.

Notes from reading the real apps while drawing: the provider and customer phone apps do not bundle the Lufga font, so on a phone they show the phone's own font (drawn here in the system font). The admin web app also renders in the system font. Photo walls use the apps' own photographs, shrunk to keep this file small. Nothing on this sheet is loaded from outside the file.
